ORAL ORDER 1. On 16.4.2024 following order was passed :-
"Learned advocate for the petitioner has submitted that present petition is based on the settlement.

sentences.text: It appears that the victim girl and accused both have got married and the victim has produced her affidavit of settlement, but a complaint is filed on behalf of respondent No.2 and there is no settlement affidavit on behalf of respondent No.2.
Therefore the question does not arise to treat this petition as a consent quashing petition.
However, it would be open for both the parties to argue this case on merits.
Stand over to 13.06.2024."
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/874/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined 2.
Pursuant to the aforesaid order, today the victim girly viz. Ashaben Bachuji Gelot is present before this Court and she is represented by learned advocate Mr. Chirag Aydi.
Learned advocate Mr.
Chirag Aydi states that the victim girl Ashaben has got married with the present applicant and they are happily married and at present are blessed with a baby girl.

Considering the fact that they are married but their marriage is not accepted by the complainant - respondent No.2 who is though served, he has chosen not to appear before this Court and therefore, considering the welfare of the couple as well as the newborn baby, the Court may quash the FIR.
3. Learned advocate Mr. Chirag Aydi has also placed on record an affidavit filed by Ashaben Bachuji Gelot on 24.12.2023.

Though the aforesaid affidavit is filed above six months and today also the victim - Ashaben Bachuji Gelot is present before this Court and she states that the Court may quash the FIR as she wants to live happily with her husband who happens to be present applicant.
4. Considering the fact that at the relevant point of time, the victim was minor.

However,
subsequently she has attained majority and has married to the present applicant and now they NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/874/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined are blessed with a baby girl and therefore, considering the welfare of the petitioner and respondent No.2 as well as welfare of the child as well as considering the fact that if, the trial for the offences for which the FIR is registered is continued, it will not serve any fruitful purpose, this Court deems it appropriate to quashed the FIR, despite the fact that the complainant's father is not present before this Court.
5. Learned advocate Mr. Chirag Aydi also points out the Marriage Certificate dated 16.10.2023.

Learned advocate Mr. Chirag Aydi also has placed on record school Leaving Certificate of the victim girl to indicate that as of today she has attained the age of majority and considering the fact that she has already delivered a baby girl and the present applicant is the father of that baby girl.
6. Heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.
Learned advocate Mr. Chirag Ayedi states that he has received instructions to appear on behalf of the victim and permitted to file his appearance in the registry.
Permission as prayed for is granted.
Registry is directed to accept the Vakilatnama of learned advocate Mr. Chirag Ayedi appearing for the victim.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/874/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined

sentences.text: 7. Rule.
Learned advocates appearing for the respective parties waives service of rule on behalf of the respective respondents.
8. Considering the issue involved in the present application and with consent of the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties, this application is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

9. By way of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code"), the applicant has prayed for quashing and setting aside F.I.R. bearing C.R. No.11195019220275 of 2022 dated 16.4.2022 registered with Deesa Rural Police Station,
District : Banaskantha for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(N)
of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act and for quashing charge-sheet and Special POCSO Case No.18 of 2022 pending before the learned 4th Additional District and Sessions Judge at Deesa at Banaskantha as well as all other consequential proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR qua the present applicant.
10.

11. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the State has opposed the present application and submitted that considering the seriousness of the offence, the complaint in question may not be quashed and the present application may be rejected.
12. Original victim - Ashaben Gelot is present in person before the Court and is identified by learned advocate for learned advocate Mr. Chirag Ayedi appearing for the original victim.
It is therefore submitted that the present application may be allowed.

13. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties, considering the facts and circumstances arising out of the present application as well as taking into consideration the decisions rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab &
Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 31,
Manoj Sharma Vs. State & Ors., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 190 and Narinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported in 2014 (2) Crime 67 (SC), it NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/874/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined appears that further continuation of criminal proceedings in relation to the impugned FIR against the applicant would be unnecessary harassment to the applicant.
